science.title: Current understanding of the NLRC4 Inflammasome in autoinflammation and enterocolitis
science.description: The NLRC4 inflammasome is a cytosolic immune sensor that detects bacterial virulence structures and rapidly initiates inflammatory responses. While tightly regulated NLRC4 activation is essential for host defense, genetic mutations that enhance NLRC4 signaling can drive severe autoinflammatory disease. Studies in patients and genetically engineered mouse models have begun to reveal how dysregulated NLRC4 activation disrupts intestinal and systemic immune homeostasis. This review summarizes current insights into NLRC4-associated autoinflammatory diseases, with particular emphasis on the mechanisms underlying autoinflammation with infantile enterocolitis, and highlights emerging concepts related to disease heterogeneity and therapeutic targeting. This mini-review summarizes how dysregulated NLRC4 inflammasome activation disrupts immune homeostasis, driving autoinflammation with enterocolitis, and discusses disease mechanisms, variability, and therapeutic approaches.

science.title: Researchers Simulate Fruit Fly Brain Controlling Virtual Body
science.description: Researchers and startups have combined a published fruit-fly connectome with neural simulators and a physics body to run a full-brain emulation that produces multiple behaviors. A 2024 connectome of the adult fruit fly, reported to contain roughly **125,000 neurons** and **50 million** synapses, underpins the work; Phil Shiu and colleagues published predictive modelling results in Nature. Reporting by Futurism and The Register describes San Francisco startup **Eon Systems** putting a connectome-based emulation into an embodied simulation so the virtual fly walks, grooms, and feeds in a simple environment. The Register credits the stack to `Brian2` and `NeuroMechFly`, while Berkeley reports the original model predicted taste-driven neural activation in the Nature paper. Coverage frames the demonstration as scientifically grounded but also a lightning rod for ethical and conceptual debates about whole-brain emulation.

science.title: GWAS reveal SUBER GENE1-mediated suberization via type one phosphatases
science.description: Suberin deposition in the root endodermis is critical for plant nutrient acquisition and environmental adaptation. Here we used an unbiased forward genetic approach based on natural variation across 284 Arabidopsis thaliana accessions to identify novel regulators of endodermal suberization. This screen revealed striking diversity in suberin levels and patterns, uncovering broader roles for suberin beyond those observed in the reference accession Col-0. A genome-wide association study pinpointed SUBER GENE1 (SBG1), a previously uncharacterized gene encoding a 129-amino-acid protein, as a key regulator of suberin deposition. SBG1 acts through physical interaction with type one protein phosphatases (TOPPs) via conserved SILK and RVxF motifs. Disrupting this interaction abolishes SBG1 function, while topp mutants exhibit enhanced endodermal suberization, mirroring SBG1 overexpression. Our findings uncover a previously unknown regulatory module linking suberin formation to TOPP activity and abscisic acid signalling, and provide a framework for improving plant stress resilience through targeted manipulation of root barrier properties. A genetic screen across Arabidopsis accessions identifies SBG1 as a regulator of root abscisic acid response and endodermal suberin deposition via type 1 protein phosphatases, revealing how natural variation shapes root barriers and stress responses.
